analysis.title: The Miners Take the Lead: What's Driving Gold & Silver Equities (Webcast, October 20, 2026)
key_insights: Gold is consolidating after an all-time high of $5,595/oz in January, which Sprott attributes to central bank buying and Asian demand. Sprott says gold has held up despite a hostile macro backdrop and that ETF demand has picked up during the correction.
Gold has risen to much higher prices despite positive 5-year real yields since March 2022. Sprott says this means investors should look beyond interest rates when assessing gold.

Central banks' US dollar-denominated reserves fell from 65% in 2006 to 57% in Q2 2026. Gold's share of reserves rose from 11% to 31%. Central bank gold purchases slowed in Q1 2026 and rebounded strongly in Q2.

Sprott argues US public debt above $40T supports gold. Since 1980, above-ground gold has grown at a 1.82% CAGR against 9.02% for US government debt. The investable gold float is about $9T, against global equities above $152T and debt of $350T.
New gold discoveries are less frequent despite record exploration spending. Sprott believes there are not enough quality deposits to sustain future production without higher gold prices.
Global gold ETF holdings have risen sharply since early 2024 but remain below the 2020 peak. Sprott sees room for further ETF demand recovery.

Silver fell about 16% year to date after a 147.95% rise in 2025, closing at $60.43/oz on 9/30/2026. The deck separately cites a $73 spot price as of 9/30/2026 on the AISC margin slide, an inconsistency in the source.
The silver market has run deficits for seven consecutive years including ETP investment. Supply grew from 1,025 Moz in 2017 to 1,090 Moz in 2025 and is forecast to fall 2% in 2026.

Silver supply is inelastic. The deck states by-product share as 74% on one slide and 67% on another. Lead/zinc (29.4%) and copper (28.0%) are the largest source metals for 2025 silver mine output, and primary silver is 26.1%.
The Shanghai silver premium is $8.67/oz. Sprott reads this as physical silver being scarce where demand is strongest.
Gold miners trade at a GDM/XAU ratio of 0.61 against a period average of 0.485. Sprott still calls the equities undervalued relative to bullion and says multiples remain below prior cycle peaks.
Gold miners (GDM) EV/EBITDA is 6.76x against 15.34x for the S&P 500. Net debt/EBITDA is -0.16 against 1.50, profit margin is 30.80% against 16.59%, and dividend yield is 1.73% against 1.11%.

Since the start of 2024, 2027 EPS expectations for gold miners are up 331% while GDM share prices are up 202% and gold is up 102%. Sprott takes this to mean miners have room to rise to meet earnings expectations.

Gold M&A is subdued despite record gold prices. Four deals account for about 86% of YTD 2026 M&A value of about US$12B: Genesis Minerals/Vault Minerals ($3.9B), Equinox Gold/Orla Mining ($5.1B), Agnico Eagle/Rupert Resources (~C$2.9B) and G Mining Ventures/G2 Goldfields (C$3.0B). Sprott expects consolidation to accelerate.
Silver producers trade at about 1.3x P/NAV while margins were $17.30/oz in 2025 and spot implies roughly $27/oz. Primary silver mines' 2025 AISC of $12.21/oz implies an 83% margin at $73 silver.

Gold and silver miners show low to moderate correlation to the S&P 500 (0.30 gold miners, 0.43 silver miners) and a negative correlation to the US dollar (-0.52 and -0.55). Sprott frames this as diversification.

sector_views.rationale: Sprott cites a gap between production costs and gold prices that gives some of the widest free cash flow spreads in the industry's history. It also cites below-peak multiples, healthy balance sheets, EPS upgrades and accelerating M&A.

Producers trade at about 1.3x P/NAV despite high margins and a persistent supply deficit. Sprott says miners are undervalued relative to silver bullion and advises a targeted approach because most silver is mined as a by-product.

earnings_insights: Gold miners' 2027 EPS consensus (Bloomberg, GDM constituents) is up 331% since the start of 2024, against a 202% rise in GDM share prices as of 9/30/2026. These are consensus estimates, not reported results.

Gold miners' free cash flow per share is shown at about $130 for 2026 on the Bloomberg GDM series as of 9/30/2026, the highest in the 2004-2026 series. The deck does not say whether 2026 is an estimate.
Silver miner margins were $17.30/oz in 2025 (reported). Spot prices imply roughly $27/oz, per Sprott.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Gold is consolidating below the January high and ETF demand is picking up.

macro_indicators.reading: $60.43/oz close on 9/30/2026, down about 16% YTD after +147.95% in 2025
macro_indicators.interpretation: Silver has corrected year to date. The deck also cites $73 silver spot on 9/30/2026 on another slide, so the figure conflicts within the source.

macro_indicators.reading: Slowed in Q1 2026 and rebounded strongly in Q2
macro_indicators.interpretation: Sprott reads central bank buying as a continuing strategic reserve shift away from the US dollar.
Reserve diversification toward gold, whose share rose from 11% to 31%.

macro_indicators.reading: Seventh consecutive annual deficit including ETPs
macro_indicators.interpretation: Demand growth against stagnant supply supports silver.
Supply is flat to falling and mining output responds little to price.
Sprott links electrification and AI data center demand to industrial silver use.

risk_factors: Past performance disclaimers apply. Sprott notes precious metals can lose value and that gold and silver prices can fluctuate substantially over short periods.
Silver output is mostly by-product (74% on one slide, 67% on another), so higher silver prices may not raise production at non-primary mines.
Permitting, geopolitical and environmental risks in mining jurisdictions can outweigh mineralization concerns.
Gold miner returns show large dispersion, which makes stock selection important.
charts_described: Gold Miners (GDM) free cash flow per share series 2004-2026 ends at $130, with earlier values of $80 and $32 in the final years listed.
The GDM/XAU ratio chart shows 0.61 against a period average of 0.485.
The deck's GDM vs S&P 500 comparison table shows EV/EBITDA of 6.76x vs 15.34x and profit margin of 30.80% vs 16.59%.
The central bank reserves chart states USD-denominated reserves fell from 65% to 57% while gold rose from 11% to 31% from 2006 to Q2 2026.
The gold vs 5-year real yield chart is split at Feb 2022/Mar 2022, with the text saying gold has risen despite positive real yields.
vol_and_positioning: Gold miners have a GDM/XAU ratio of 0.61 against a 2017-2026 average of 0.485.
Sprott says the gold mining sector is underrepresented in portfolios, so modest inflows could drive outsized performance.
Gold ETF holdings are rebuilding but remain below the 2020 peak.
geopolitical: The deck cites a Wall Street Journal October 15, 2026 item on protesters gathering near the venue of the IMF meetings in Bangkok, presented as part of a hostile macro backdrop.
Sprott notes geopolitical risk as one driver of central bank diversification away from the US dollar.
